observation_summary: The compiler incorrectly reports a type mismatch when a variable is marked @const and initialized with a type-cast. The type system fails to recognize the casted type, instead inferring a different type from the object literal, causing downstream validation errors.
hypothesis: The compiler fails to correctly propagate the type information when a variable is marked as @const and initialized with a type-cast. Specifically, in TypedScopeCreator, the logic for determining the type of a constant variable does not prioritize the explicit type-cast information provided in the JSDoc of the rValue, leading to a type mismatch error when the constant is later used.
prediction: The fix in TypedScopeCreator will involve checking for JSDoc type information on the rValue before falling back to the inferred type, ensuring that the explicit type-cast is respected for @const variables.
experiment_rationale: The provided fix diff clearly shows that the logic in TypedScopeCreator was updated to prioritize JSDoc type information (rValueInfo.getType()) over the inferred rValue.getJSType() when evaluating constant types. This is a procedural correction in how the compiler determines the type of a constant, fitting the Algorithm/Method category.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a failure to correctly implement the type resolution logic for constants with type casts. The fix modifies the procedure for evaluating the type of a constant in TypedScopeCreator to correctly prioritize explicit JSDoc type information. This is a local procedural change to the type inference algorithm.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The issue is not a missing guard or validation check, but rather an incorrect implementation of the type resolution algorithm for constants.
While it involves initialization, the core issue is the logic used to determine the type during that initialization, which is an algorithmic/procedural concern.
